settings.title: How We Keep Your Home Warm, Safe, and Efficient

settings.editor: Whether you need a quick repair on a freezing night or want to plan ahead for a new heating system this year, we have you covered:

Heaters have a habit of shutting down on the coldest night of the year, and never on a mild afternoon. When you are bundling up to stay warm, you need your system fixed quickly. Our vans arrive fully stocked with common parts so we can get to the bottom of the real issue and get your home cozy again on the spot.

If your current system is over 12 to 15 years old, breaks down often, or struggles to keep your home warm, upgrading can save you the chills as well as hundreds on your utility bills. Plus, we do the real math on your home’s square footage so you get a system that fits just right.

Why wait for a winter heating emergency when you could avoid one altogether in September? Think of our fall tune-up as an annual check-up for your heater. We clear away summer dust, test safety switches, check for heat exchanger cracks, and make sure your system won’t stutter the second temperatures drop.

Because heat pumps work year-round by cooling all summer and heating all winter, they require specialized care. We inspect outdoor coils, test defrost cycles, and balance auxiliary heat strips so you don’t have to worry about your electric bill sending a shiver down your spine.

settings.title: Heating Systems We Service, Repair & Install

settings.editor: Every home in Central North Carolina is built a little differently. Some neighborhoods in Raleigh and Wake Forest have natural gas lines, while homes in Louisburg and rural Franklin County often rely on electric heat pumps or delivered propane. No matter what kind of system warms your home, our certified technicians have the tools and experience to service it right:

As North Carolina’s go-to heating choice, heat pumps handle both summer humidity and winter chills without the need for two separate systems. Whether you have a traditional central unit, a ductless mini-split, or a high-efficiency variable-speed system, we keep the heat moving efficiently without wasting electricity.

A gas furnace delivers fast, toasty heat through your vents. Because we are licensed in both HVAC and plumbing, we safely service gas valves, burner assemblies, ignitors, flame sensors, and exhaust flues to keep your home warm and safe from carbon monoxide leaks.

A dual-fuel system pairs an electric heat pump with a gas furnace backup. It uses the heat pump on mild 70° days and switches over to gas heat during winter freezes. We install and service hybrid systems to give you the lowest possible monthly heating bill.

Do you have a garage that feels like a walk-in freezer, or a bonus room that makes you immediately grab a blanket? A mini-split gives you fast, quiet heat in those chilly rooms, without messing with the rest of the house or starting a thermostat argument.

settings.title: Is Your Heater Acting Up? 5 Signs It’s Time to Give Us a Call

settings.editor: Most heating problems give you a few signs before the entire system stops working. If you notice any of these issues, giving us a call now can prevent an expensive emergency breakdown later:

🥶 Cool or lukewarm air — rooms never reach the temperature you set.

🔊 Loud sounds — screeching, banging, persistent clicking, or rattling while it runs.

👃 Odd smells — burning plastic, sulfur, or a heavy damp smell that lingers in the air.

⏱️ Short-cycling — the system shuts off after only two or three minutes.

💸 A power bill that spikes out of nowhere, without a big change in the weather.
Don’t wait for a total breakdown on the coldest night of the year. Let our team take a look and fix the small stuff before it becomes a big problem.

settings.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Home Heating

items.item_title: How do I know if I have a heat pump or a furnace?
How much does heating repair or replacement cost with Dolan Design?
How often should my heating system be serviced?
Is a heat pump better than a gas furnace in North Carolina?
What does it mean when “Aux Heat” turns on?
How long does a typical home heating system last?

settings.editor: Look at your outdoor unit in the winter. If it runs when you turn on the heat, you have a heat pump. If it only turns on in the summer for AC and your indoor heater runs on gas, you have a furnace.

Repairs start with a simple, flat diagnostic fee to find the problem. Replacements depend on your home’s size, but we always give you an exact, upfront price with zero hidden fees before we touch a thing.
Once a year in the early fall months. A quick pre-winter tune-up catches worn parts before they break, keeps your power bills low, and protects your warranty.

It depends on your setup. Heat pumps are usually cheaper to run in our mild NC winters, but gas furnaces give you faster, warmer heat on super cold nights. Many local homeowners actually use both in a hybrid system.

It means your heat pump called in backup power, like electric heating strips, because it’s freezing outside or you raised the thermostat by several degrees. If it stays on during mild weather above 45°F, give us a call.
Heat pumps usually last 12 to 15 years because they work year-round for both heating and cooling. Standalone gas furnaces can last 15 to 20 years since they only run a few months out of the year.
